name: Hue & Cry
oneLiner: A colour-first hair salon on King Street, Newtown — corrections, balayage, gloss and vivids, all spoken in the colourist's own numbered language.

axes.secondaryReason: the shade-card/formula print grammar (numbered chapters, level scales, mono formula lines) is the supporting flavour that makes the palette axis read as craft

paletteSeed: five pigment worlds, one per chapter, each mixed tone-on-tone from a single hue family — copper 7.44 (apricot paper, sienna ink), honey 8.3, rose 9.26, violet 5.20, blue-black 1.1 as the lights-off close; the scroll travels the shade chart through adjacent families, and with JS the paper itself takes the dye between chapters (OKLab mixing)
typeDirection: Bodoni Moda variable (fashion-didone display, italic flourishes) + Schibsted Grotesk (humanist body) + Chivo Mono (the tint-number/formula register) — all OFL, vendored
motionBudget: scroll is the instrument: the fixed dye layer cross-fades between chapter pigments as you scroll (OKLab lerp, rAF); the hero band develops in once like dye processing; cards rise gently on entry; the shade rail tracks the active chapter; the mixer paints its shade onto a real photographed head of hair (masked CSS blend layers) and answers instantly. Reduced motion: hard chapter boundaries, everything pre-developed and visible. No-JS: complete content with fixed per-chapter colours and the natural-hair photo
